title: Understanding KDE Normalization
text: When creating a Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) plot, normalization ensures that the area under the curve sums to $$1$$. This is important for interpreting the plot as a probability density function. If the KDE is not normalized, it might not accurately represent the distribution of the data.

hintAnswer: The plot may not accurately represent the probability density.
title: Effect of Normalization on KDE
text: What is the effect of not normalizing the kernel in a KDE plot?
choices: The plot may not accurately represent the probability density.
The plot will look like a normal distribution.
The plot will have more peaks.

title: Multimodal Distributions
text: A multimodal distribution has multiple peaks. If your KDE plot looks like a normal distribution, it might be due to the choice of bandwidth or kernel, not necessarily the normalization.

hintAnswer: The choice of bandwidth or kernel might be incorrect.
title: Identifying Issues with KDE
text: If a KDE plot of a multimodal distribution looks like a normal distribution, what could be a possible reason?
choices: The choice of bandwidth or kernel might be incorrect.
The data is actually normally distributed.
